title: Dry-run stepwise switchover and graceful-degradation playbook for active-passive DR
creator: Aisha Morales
description: Purpose: Create a repeatable, low-risk dry-run playbook that exercises an orderly active->passive switchover, validates backup/restore integrity, and rehearses graceful degradation (circuit breakers + load shedding) without impacting production customers. Background: Recent regional incidents revealed gaps in staged traffic reduction and KV cache resync timing. This ticket consolidates runbook steps, verification harnesses, monitoring checks, and the scheduled drill cadence for verification across teams (serving runtime, infra, console, oncall). Scope: - One full dry-run (no public traffic cut) against mirror traffic and synthetic workloads. - Validate backup/restore for tokenstore and model metadata snapshots. - Exercise circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding policies in controlled manner. - Produce a post-drill checklist and remediation items. Out-of-scope: full manual customer DNS TTL changes, consumer-facing mass failovers, or changes to SLA commitments.
tasks: Define dry-run success criteria and acceptance tests
Instrument mirror traffic pipeline and synthetic load generator
Add temporary feature flags for staged traffic siphon and cache freeze
Implement automated backup checksum validation for tokenstore and metadata
Create rollback/abort hooks and a single-touch abort play in runbook
Coordinate calendar and run participants (SRE, runtime, console, infra)
Run tabletop and preflight checks three days before drill
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run completes without production request rate reduction (mirror traffic only) and all steps validated
Backup snapshotted files verified with checksums and restored into an isolated staging cluster
KV cache warmup/snapshot/resync timings recorded and within target windows
Circuit breakers tripped at configured thresholds and automatic fallback engaged as expected
Load-shedding policies evict best-effort low-priority routes and preserve core SLO-bearing routes
Post-drill report produced with action items, owners, and timelines
runbook_summary: High-level flow: 1) Preflight checks (SLO health, backlog, disk, quotas) 2) Snapshot backups (tokenstore, model-metadata, routing-table) 3) Mirror traffic cutover to passive region using siphon (no production reduction) 4) Trigger staged circuit-breakers and observe degradations 5) Validate backup restores into isolated cluster and run smoke tests 6) Resync KV caches and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies 7) Roll back mirror traffic and remove feature flags 8) Post-mortem and action tracking

monitoring_changes: Add temporary dashboard: DR Drill - Mirror Run (latency, error-rate, kv-resync, restore-time)
Alert: DR-Preflight-Fail if any SLO > 25% error budget burn in last 1h
Synthetic checks: end-to-end generation, embedding store reads, model load times
Trace spans: tag drill-run-id to correlate traces across regions
circuit_breaker_config: Primary threshold: 5xx rate > 3% over 1m -> trip (local region)
Secondary threshold: p99 latency > 2.5s for 2 consecutive 1m windows -> trip
Open state action: route traffic to passive mirror or activate fallback-model variant
Half-open probe: allow 1% of requests through for 30s and evaluate success rate
load_shedding_policy: Shedding order: evict low-tier routes, then throttle medium-tier, preserve core-tier until critical
Throttle rate: reduce medium-tier QPS by 50% per level with exponential backoff
Metrics to watch: queue-lengths, retry-rates, consumer-backpressure indicators
backup_validation_plan: Run backup snapshot and compute SHA256 checksums for tokenstore and model metadata
Restore snapshot into isolated cluster (dry-run env) and run integrated smoke tests
Verify idempotence by repeating restore and checking for deterministic state
Run data-integrity queries: record counts, hash of key lists, and selective object fetches
Record RTO/RPO timings and compare to target: RTO < 15m for control-plane metadata, RTO < 2h for large artifacts
